text:
Maria: Quick idea — I think our kernel selector + stochastic batching heuristic is getting biased when we feed replay traffic with bursty inter-arrival patterns. Could explain the p99 regressions we saw yesterday.
Jake: oof. which replay trace? the customer X one? :thinking: 
Maria: Not that one. I used a sampled production trace from last week (mixed tenants). But I also tried a Poisson synth that matched mean rate and the tail behavior diverges.
Sophia: divergence how? throughput down or tail up?
Maria: tail latency up (p95->p99) and batch size variance very high. Also KV cache hit ratio drops ~12% during microbursts, so more attention misses.
Lee: hmm KV pollution could be from unfair queueing — big tenants filling cache and evicting small-tenant prefixes. Do you have measurements?
Maria: pasted a quick summary from the run: 
```
run_id=stoch-replay-2026-03-18
traffic=sampled-prod-50k-requests
synth_mode=poisson(mean=12r/s, cv=1.8)
metrics: p50=45ms p95=190ms p99=420ms
batch_stats: mean=8 median=6 p95=24 p99=40
kv_hit: baseline=82% during steady -> 70% during bursts
kernel_choice: mostly int8-kernel-v2 then fallback to fp16-kernel-v1 on long seqs
```

Jake: Interesting kernel flip. Is the selector using sequence-length + memory pressure? That fallback can change per-token latencies a lot.
Sophia: Also continuous batching delay cap might be letting some requests wait too long to form bigger batches; elastic delay tradeoff. If that cap is per-tenant we need to check fairness.
Maria: I reproduced with a tighter max_delay=5ms and saw p95 drop ~30ms but throughput slightly down. With max_delay=20ms p95 improves but p99 unchanged.
Lee: Can you share the exact harness configs? I'll run a focused test with isolated tenants to see eviction patterns.
Maria: config I used: 
```
replay_harness:
  sample_trace: "mixed-prod-sample-2026-03-10.json"
  replay_speed: "1x"
  traffic_model: "poisson"
  batching:
    strategy: "stochastic"
    max_delay_ms: 12
    batch_size_cap: 64
  kernel_selector:
    policy: "latency_cost" # cost-based with fallback
    prefer_quantized: true
  kv_cache:
    size_mb: 1024
    eviction: "lru_per_tenant"
```

BenchBot: Starting run stoch-replay-2026-03-18 (id=8791). Expected duration ~15m. Logs -> gs://bench-archive/stoch-replay-8791/
Jake: can we also run an apples->apples synthetic that replicates the burst autocorrelation? Poisson won't capture burst clustering. Maybe a Weibull or on/off Pareto submodel.
Sophia: Good call. I can generate a clustered arrival model: on periods 200-500ms with 30-60r/s, off periods 2-6s. That should stress cache and kernel warm paths.
Maria: yes please. Also add a variant with kernel_selector policy="throughput_cost" and one with prefer_quantized=false so we can see kernel flip effects.
Lee: I'll instrument KV cache per-prefix eviction counts and tenant-wise live prefixes. Want a CSV output for heatmap plotting.
Maria: added a small log snippet from the first 3 minutes: 
```
[00:01:12] tenant=A batch=18 latency=120ms kv_hit=65% kernel=int8-v2
[00:01:13] tenant=B batch=2 latency=310ms kv_hit=20% kernel=fp16-v1
[00:01:14] tenant=A batch=22 latency=95ms kv_hit=68% kernel=int8-v2
[00:01:15] tenant=C batch=1 latency=480ms kv_hit=8% kernel=fp16-v1
```

Jake: wow tenant C getting singletons and high tail. That smells like global queueing favoring big tenants. Are we using weighted round-robin or strict priority?
Sophia: For continuous batching we currently have a global delay budget and a per-tenant min-throughput hint but queueing is mostly first-come-first-served with opportunistic fairness.
Lee: That opportunistic fairness might starve small tenants during bursts. Proposal: add a sliding-window tenant fairness score that boosts effective priority when a tenant sees rising tail.
Maria: Love that. For experiments let's keep three axes: (1) traffic model (poisson / clustered / replay sample), (2) batching params (max_delay 5/12/20, cap 32/64), (3) selector policy (latency_cost / throughput_cost) + quantized toggle. Run grid and collect p50/p95/p99, throughput, kv_hit per-tenant.
BenchBot: run matrix queued: 3x3x4 = 36 experiments. ETA ~4 hours on bench pool.
Jake: Add a baseline with cache disabled (kv_cache.size_mb=0) to validate cache contribution.
Maria: done. Also flagging this as a perf-regression hypothesis from yday's canary. ops, please hold canary while we confirm? @OpsBot 
OpsBot: Canary hold requested by Maria. Notified on-call and paused new canaries for 1h. :white_check_mark:
Sophia: If matrix finishes we should plot tenant-level delta in kv_hit vs p99 and kernel-switch timestamps overlayed. That should tell if kernel flips align with eviction windows.
Lee: I'll collate the CSVs into a notebook and run a cross-correlation between eviction spikes and kernel_fallback events.
Maria: thanks. If we see kernel fallback following eviction consistently we might change selector to prefer kernel stability over one-shot latency.
Jake: or we could pre-warm fp16 kernels for tenants that have seen recent eviction to avoid per-request fallback. Tradeoff analysis needed.
Sophia: Agreed. For now let the bench run. Any quick Qs?
Lee: one: are we measuring CPU scheduler interference on host? Sometimes kernel switching is due to co-runner swapping GPU context.
Maria: good point — I'll enable host perf counters and nvml GPU context churn logs.
BenchBot: run stoch-replay-8791 -> completed. Summary (36 runs): median p95 delta across matrix = +28ms vs baseline. Full csv: gs://bench-archive/stoch-replay-8791/results.csv
Maria: pulling results now. Early glance: clustered traffic + max_delay=12 + prefer_quantized=true shows worst p99 for small tenants.
Jake: can you drop one example plot in the channel when you have it?
Maria: will do. Uploading kernel-switch overlay and tenant kv-heatmap in 5m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
